Parameter UI module

Source: R/ui_params_module.R
pub_params_ui.Rd

A Shiny module that shows a compact table with one input per param (pub_param_input()) and checks every change with the validity functions of the params (param_validity()).

Usage

pub_params_ui(id)

pub_params_server(
  id,
  params,
  on_invalid = c("restore", "keep"),
  update_on = c("blur", "change"),
  group_by = "area",
  group_labels = NULL,
  width = "15ch",
  tooltips = TRUE,
  reset = FALSE
)

pub_pipeline_params_server(
  id,
  pip,
  on_invalid = c("restore", "keep"),
  update_on = c("blur", "change"),
  group_by = "area",
  group_labels = NULL,
  width = "15ch",
  tooltips = TRUE,
  reset = FALSE,
  filter = list(),
  refresh = NULL
)

Arguments

id

character(1) module id, the same as in pub_params_ui().

params

A reactive returning a named list (or param_config()) of param objects.

on_invalid

"restore": an invalid input gets back the last valid value; "keep": it keeps the invalid value and valid() is FALSE.

update_on

"blur": text and numeric inputs report a change on blur or Enter; "change": on every keystroke (after a short delay).

group_by

character(1) name of the attribute that groups the params, or NULL.

group_labels

Named character vector or list of group headings, e.g. c(analysis = "Analysis parameters", report = "Report parameters").

width

Width of the inputs (CSS), e.g. "15ch", or NULL. The inputs of a param_group() share it.

tooltips

TRUE: show the description of a param as tooltip of its input.

reset

TRUE: add a button that sets all inputs back to their initial values (see "Resetting values").

pip

A pipeflow pipeline or view, or a reactive returning one.

filter

Optional named list of attribute filters that is passed to pub_get_params(), e.g., list(source = "user") is called with pub_get_params(pip, source = "user"). The default list() shows all params of the pipeline. See "Parameter filters" in the examples of pub_get_params().

refresh

NULL or a reactive: whenever it fires, the params are read again from the pipeline. Use it after code outside the module changed the pipeline.

Value

  • pub_params_ui(): a tag list with the container of the table and pubflow's HTML dependency (JavaScript and CSS).

  • pub_params_server(): a list of reactives:

    • values: named list of the current valid plain values (NULL before the params are available);

    • changed: named list of the values that changed (and are valid) with the latest change; NULL before the first change;

    • valid: TRUE if no input holds an invalid value (only FALSE with on_invalid = "keep").

  • pub_pipeline_params_server(): the same as pub_params_server() plus:

    • revision: an integer that goes up by one whenever the module has updated the params in the pipeline (that is, pipeflow::pip_set_params() succeeded). Usually, it is used to trigger a pipeline run that updates the results.

Details

Functions

  • pub_params_ui() is the UI part: place it where the table should appear.

  • pub_params_server() takes a reactive that returns the params, e.g. a param_config().

  • pub_pipeline_params_server() reads the params from a pipeline with pub_get_params() and sets every valid change in the pipeline with pipeflow::pip_set_params() (see "Setting params" in pub_get_params()).

Given a view, e.g. pipeflow::pip_view(p, tags = "analysis"), pub_pipeline_params_server() shows the params of the view's steps only. It sets their values in every step of the pipeline that has them, also outside the view, so that a param keeps one value.

Layout

  • The rows follow the order of the config (attribute order, see param_config()), then the given order.

  • If more than one value of the attribute group_by occurs, each group gets a heading (from group_labels, else the value). Params without the attribute come under "Other".

  • Params with advanced = TRUE go into a collapsed "Advanced" block of their group.

  • Input ids are ns(<name>), for param groups ns(<name>_<child>).

Updates

The table is only rendered again if the structure of the params changes (names, types, choices or attributes other than the validity functions, also locked). If only values change, e.g. after a data-derived value was set in the pipeline, the inputs are updated in place.

Validation

Text and numeric inputs report their value on blur or Enter (update_on = "blur"), other inputs immediately. The value is converted to the type of the param (an empty numeric input becomes NA) and validated:

  • A valid value is emitted in changed and values.

  • An invalid value is shown next to the input (the first message, for about 3 s) and the input glows. The message "'<label>' input: <message>" is also logged with message() as an audit trail. What happens to the input depends on on_invalid:

    • "restore": it gets back its last valid value;

    • "keep": it keeps the invalid value, which does not reach values, and valid() is FALSE until the input is valid again.

  • If a param group fails its own rule (e.g. lower limit below upper limit, see add_validity()), the child input that was changed is marked.

Locked params

Params with locked = TRUE are shown as disabled inputs (see pub_param_input()), so their values only come from params().

  • The server ignores changes of their inputs (logged as "'<label>' input: locked, change ignored") and the input gets back its value.

  • The reset button leaves them alone.

  • pub_pipeline_params_server() also locks the params of a locked step (pipeflow::pip_lock()), also a step outside the view: pip_set_params() skips locked steps, so a change would leave the steps of the same name with different values. New step locks are noticed when the params are read again (refresh).

Resetting values

With reset = TRUE a button sets all inputs back to their initial values: the values in params(). Locked params are left alone.

  • If params() returns new values (e.g. data-derived defaults after a run), these are the new initial values.

  • Values that only come back from the pipeline after a change by the user (with refresh, or after it rejected a value) are not new initial values, so the button still restores the values from before the user's changes.

  • If the validity rules of a param changed in the meantime and its initial value no longer passes them, that input is not reset. The user sees the validity message, as for a rejected input, and the input keeps its value. E.g. the user set n from 1 to 2, then params() gave n a new rule "at least 2" with the same value 2: the reset to 1 would break it.

Rejected values

If pipeflow::pip_set_params() fails (pipeflow_set_params_error, e.g. because the pipeline holds stricter params than the ones read before), the input is treated like an invalid one and shows the pipeline's value again.

See also

pub_param_input(), pub_get_params()

Examples

cfg <- param_config(
    alpha = numeric_param(0.05, label = "Alpha", min = 0, max = 0.5,
                          area = "analysis"),
    trans = choice_param("none", choices = c("none", "log"),
                         label = "Transformation", area = "analysis"),
    title = param("Report", label = "Title", area = "report")
)

ui <- shiny::fluidPage(
    shiny::sidebarLayout(
        shiny::sidebarPanel(pub_params_ui("params")),
        shiny::mainPanel(shiny::verbatimTextOutput("values"))
    )
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
    params <- pub_params_server("params", shiny::reactive(cfg),
                                reset = TRUE)
    output$values <- shiny::renderPrint(str(params$values()))
}
if (interactive()) shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)

# Parameters of a pipeline
pip <- pipeflow::pip_new("demo") |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("fit", \(alpha = 0.05) alpha)
pipeflow::pip_set_params(pip, param_config(
    alpha = numeric_param(0.05, label = "Alpha", min = 0, max = 0.5,
                          source = "user")
), unknown = "error")
server <- function(input, output, session) {
    params <- pub_pipeline_params_server("params", pip)
    output$values <- shiny::renderPrint({
        params$revision()
        pipeflow::pip_run(pip, lgr = NULL)
        pip[["fit", "out"]]
    })
}
if (interactive()) shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)
